title: GitHub - shaqkao/screenshotify: Automatically turn screenshots into meaningful filenames with AI.
excerpt: Automatically turn screenshots into meaningful filenames with AI. - shaqkao/screenshotify
content_html:
Your screenshots folder, but the filenames make sense.

Screenshotify sits in the Windows tray or the macOS menu bar, notices new screenshots, and asks an AI model of your choosing for a filename that describes what is actually on screen. Nothing is renamed until you say so.

Free · open source · MIT · bring your own API key

Why

Screenshot 2026-08-12 143507.png tells you NOTHING. Six months later you have four hundred of them and no way to find the one you need.

Existing AI renamers are manual batch tools, subscription products, or both. Screenshotify is the combination that did not exist: open source, free, focused on screenshots, and genuinely watching in the background.

What it does

  • Watches your screenshot folders. New screenshots are picked up automatically, once the file has finished being written.
  • Suggests, never assumes. Every suggestion lands in a review list. Confirm, edit, or skip. Undo is always available, including after a restart.
  • Renames what you already have. Point it at a folder of old screenshots and it queues every one of them into the same review list.
  • Runs on the model you choose. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including ones running entirely on your own machine.
  • Stays out of the way. Windows tray icon or macOS menu bar item, optional start-at-login, and closing the window hides it rather than quitting.

Bring your own model

Screenshotify has no backend and no account. You point it at an endpoint and it uses your key. Anything OpenAI-compatible that accepts image input works:

Provider Base URL Notes
OpenAI https://api.openai.com/v1 gpt-4o-mini is a good default
OpenRouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 One key, many vision models
Ollama http://localhost:11434/v1 Fully local, no key needed
LM Studio http://localhost:1234/v1 Fully local, no key needed
vLLM / LiteLLM your own URL Anything speaking the same API

The model field is free text — type whatever your endpoint accepts. It must be a model that can see images (gpt-4o-mini, qwen2.5vl, llava, …).

"OpenAI-compatible" is a loose promise, and plenty of endpoints accept the chat schema while rejecting images. Settings → Test connection sends a small real image so you find out immediately rather than on your first screenshot.

Running it entirely offline

Point the base URL at Ollama or LM Studio and no image ever leaves your machine. This is the same feature as "local model support" in other tools — Screenshotify just does not try to manage the model runtime for you.

Privacy

  • Screenshots are sent only to the endpoint you configure, only when a suggestion is needed, and downscaled first (1024 px longest edge by default).
  • Your API key is stored in the Windows Credential Manager or the macOS Keychain, never in a config file, and is never handed back to the app's UI layer — requests are made from the Rust process.
  • No telemetry, no analytics, no accounts, no server.

Installing

Download the installer for your platform from the latest release and run it. That single file is everything — there is no runtime to install alongside it, no Node, no Python, no account.

Screenshotify is a native app built with Tauri, so it renders its UI with the webview the OS already ships — WebView2 on Windows, WebKit on macOS — instead of bundling a copy of Chromium the way an Electron app does. That is the difference between a download measured in single-digit megabytes and one measured in hundreds.

Windows

Screenshotify_x64-setup.exe. On the rare machine without WebView2, the installer fetches it automatically.

Screenshotify is not yet code-signed, so Windows will show "Windows protected your PC" the first time you run the installer. This is normal for new, unsigned open-source software — the warning is about the absence of a paid certificate, not about anything found in the file. Click More info, then Run anyway.

A code-signing certificate through the SignPath Foundation free-for-open-source programme is being applied for; once granted, releases will be signed automatically and this warning will disappear.

macOS 10.15 or newer

Screenshotify_universal.dmg — one file for both Apple Silicon and Intel. Open it, drag Screenshotify to Applications, then right-click the app → Open the first time. Builds are ad-hoc signed but not notarised, which is what that extra step is about; a plain double-click gives you a refusal with no way past it.

macOS will also ask for permission to read your screenshot folder on first run. Say yes — without it the folder is watched but unreadable, which looks like the app doing nothing at all.

docs/MACOS.md covers both of those in more detail, along with how the app behaves as a menu bar app and what to do if macOS calls the download damaged.

Using it

  1. Settings → AI provider — set the base URL, key and model, then Test connection.
  2. Settings → Watched folders — Use default Screenshots folder usually finds the right one (on macOS that is wherever ⇧⌘5 saves to, normally the Desktop).
  3. Take a screenshot. A notification appears; open Screenshotify from the tray or the menu bar to review the suggested name.
  4. Review — press Enter or click Apply on a row, or Apply all.
  5. Got an existing pile? Review → Scan a folder…

Naming options

Filename style (kebab-case, snake_case, Title Case, camelCase, spaces), an optional date prefix taken from the file's own timestamp, a word limit, the description language, and free-form extra instructions for the model — all under Settings → Naming.

Building from source

Only needed if you want to modify Screenshotify — users never install any of this. Each platform builds its own installer; there is no cross-compiling.

Windows. Compiling a native binary needs a C++ linker and the Windows SDK, so expect roughly 5 GB of one-off toolchain:

  • Node.js 20 or newer
  • Rust (stable, MSVC toolchain)
  • Visual Studio Build Tools — the Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 component is enough; the full Desktop development with C++ workload also works but installs considerably more than this project uses
  • Windows SDK (10.0.22621 or newer)
  • WebView2 runtime (already present on Windows 10/11)
winget install Rustlang.Rustup
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override `
  "--quiet --wait --norestart --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.Windows11SDK.26100"
rustup default stable

macOS. Xcode Command Line Tools, Node and Rust — a much smaller download, and the details are in docs/MACOS.md:

xcode-select --install
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh

Then, on either:

npm install
npm run start     # dev build with hot reload
npm test          # unit tests for the filename pipeline
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
npm run release   # nsis/*.exe on Windows, dmg/*.dmg on macOS

The frontend is plain HTML/CSS/JS through Vite; the backend is Rust via Tauri v2.

Project layout

index.html            single-window UI shell
src/
  main.js             bootstrap, tray/watcher events, settings form
  queue.js            review queue + bounded-concurrency AI calls
  review.js           the review list and applying renames
  history.js          persisted rename log, powers undo
  naming.js           model output -> safe filename
  naming.test.js      unit tests for the above (node --test)
  settings.js         persisted settings + credential-store key access
  platform.js         the per-platform facts the UI words itself from
src-tauri/
  src/lib.rs          commands, tray/menu bar, window behaviour
  src/watcher.rs      folder watching with write-completion detection
  src/ai.rs           OpenAI-compatible vision requests
  src/imaging.rs      downscale + JPEG + base64
  src/files.rs        scanning, collision-safe rename, undo
  src/secrets.rs      Credential Manager / Keychain
  src/toast.rs        WinRT toast on Windows, plain notification elsewhere
  tauri.conf.json     shared config, plus the Windows bundle
  tauri.macos.conf.json
                      merged over it when building for macOS
  Info.plist          macOS folder-access usage descriptions

Platform-specific behaviour is #[cfg]-gated in Rust and driven off platform.js in the frontend, so neither side sniffs the user agent or assumes a platform. docs/MACOS.md lists what differs on macOS and why.

Not in v1

Deliberately left out to keep the first release shippable:

  • Managing local models for you (installing, downloading, VRAM detection) — point the base URL at Ollama or LM Studio instead
  • Mac App Store distribution
  • Notarised macOS builds (they need a paid Apple Developer ID)
  • Linux — the Rust side is #[cfg]-gated rather than Windows-only now, but nothing there has been built or tested
  • File types other than images

These may be implemented in the future, who knows?

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. The most useful contributions right now are real-world reports of endpoints or models that misbehave, and screenshots that produce bad names.

License

MIT — see LICENSE.

content_html_zh:
Your screenshots folder, but the filenames make sense.

Screenshotify sits in the Windows tray or the macOS menu bar, notices new screenshots, and asks an AI model of your choosing for a filename that describes what is actually on screen. Nothing is renamed until you say so.

Free · open source · MIT · bring your own API key

Why

Screenshot 2026-08-12 143507.png tells you NOTHING. Six months later you have four hundred of them and no way to find the one you need.

Existing AI renamers are manual batch tools, subscription products, or both. Screenshotify is the combination that did not exist: open source, free, focused on screenshots, and genuinely watching in the background.

它的作用

  • Watches your screenshot folders. New screenshots are picked up automatically, once the file has finished being written.
  • Suggests, never assumes. Every suggestion lands in a review list. Confirm, edit, or skip. Undo is always available, including after a restart.
  • Renames what you already have. Point it at a folder of old screenshots and it queues every one of them into the same review list.
  • Runs on the model you choose. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including ones running entirely on your own machine.
  • Stays out of the way. Windows tray icon or macOS menu bar item, optional start-at-login, and closing the window hides it rather than quitting.

带上你自己的模型

Screenshotify has no backend and no account. You point it at an endpoint and it uses your key. Anything OpenAI-compatible that accepts image input works:

提供者 基本网址 Notes
开放人工智能 https://api.openai.com/v1 gpt-4o-mini is a good default
开放路由器 https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 One key, many vision models
成为 http://localhost:11434/v1 Fully local, no key needed
LM工作室 http://localhost:1234/v1 Fully local, no key needed
vLLM / LiteLLM your own URL Anything speaking the same API

The model field is free text — type whatever your endpoint accepts. It must be a model that can see images (gpt-4o-mini, qwen2.5vl, llava, …).

"OpenAI-compatible" is a loose promise, and plenty of endpoints accept the chat schema while rejecting images. Settings → Test connection sends a small real image so you find out immediately rather than on your first screenshot.

Running it entirely offline

Point the base URL at Ollama or LM Studio and no image ever leaves your machine. This is the same feature as "local model support" in other tools — Screenshotify just does not try to manage the model runtime for you.

隐私

  • Screenshots are sent only to the endpoint you configure, only when a suggestion is needed, and downscaled first (1024 px longest edge by default).
  • Your API key is stored in the Windows Credential Manager or the macOS Keychain, never in a config file, and is never handed back to the app's UI layer — requests are made from the Rust process.
  • No telemetry, no analytics, no accounts, no server.

安装中

Download the installer for your platform from the latest release and run it. That single file is everything — there is no runtime to install alongside it, no Node, no Python, no account.

Screenshotify is a native app built with Tauri, so it renders its UI with the webview the OS already ships — WebView2 on Windows, WebKit on macOS — instead of bundling a copy of Chromium the way an Electron app does. That is the difference between a download measured in single-digit megabytes and one measured in hundreds.

视窗

Screenshotify_x64-setup.exe. On the rare machine without WebView2, the installer fetches it automatically.

Screenshotify is not yet code-signed, so Windows will show "Windows protected your PC" the first time you run the installer. This is normal for new, unsigned open-source software — the warning is about the absence of a paid certificate, not about anything found in the file. Click More info, then Run anyway.

A code-signing certificate through the SignPath Foundation free-for-open-source programme is being applied for; once granted, releases will be signed automatically and this warning will disappear.

macOS 10.15 or newer

Screenshotify_universal.dmg — one file for both Apple Silicon and Intel. Open it, drag Screenshotify to Applications, then right-click the app → Open the first time. Builds are ad-hoc signed but not notarised, which is what that extra step is about; a plain double-click gives you a refusal with no way past it.

macOS will also ask for permission to read your screenshot folder on first run. Say yes — without it the folder is watched but unreadable, which looks like the app doing nothing at all.

docs/MACOS.md covers both of those in more detail, along with how the app behaves as a menu bar app and what to do if macOS calls the download damaged.

使用它

  1. Settings → AI provider — set the base URL, key and model, then Test connection.
  2. Settings → Watched folders — Use default Screenshots folder usually finds the right one (on macOS that is wherever ⇧⌘5 saves to, normally the Desktop).
  3. Take a screenshot. A notification appears; open Screenshotify from the tray or the menu bar to review the suggested name.
  4. Review — press Enter or click Apply on a row, or Apply all.
  5. Got an existing pile? Review → Scan a folder…

Naming options

Filename style (kebab-case, snake_case, Title Case, camelCase, spaces), an optional date prefix taken from the file's own timestamp, a word limit, the description language, and free-form extra instructions for the model — all under Settings → Naming.

从源头构建

Only needed if you want to modify Screenshotify — users never install any of this. Each platform builds its own installer; there is no cross-compiling.

视窗。 Compiling a native binary needs a C++ linker and the Windows SDK, so expect roughly 5 GB of one-off toolchain:

  • Node.js 20 or newer
  • Rust (stable, MSVC toolchain)
  • Visual Studio Build Tools — the Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 component is enough; the full Desktop development with C++ workload also works but installs considerably more than this project uses
  • Windows SDK (10.0.22621 or newer)
  • WebView2 runtime (already present on Windows 10/11)
winget install Rustlang.Rustup
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override `
  "--quiet --wait --norestart --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.Windows11SDK.26100"
rustup default stable

macOS. Xcode Command Line Tools, Node and Rust — a much smaller download, and the details are in docs/MACOS.md:

xcode-select --install
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh

Then, on either:

npm install
npm run start     # dev build with hot reload
npm test          # unit tests for the filename pipeline
cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
npm run release   # nsis/*.exe on Windows, dmg/*.dmg on macOS

The frontend is plain HTML/CSS/JS through Vite; the backend is Rust via Tauri v2.

项目布局

index.html            single-window UI shell
src/
  main.js             bootstrap, tray/watcher events, settings form
  queue.js            review queue + bounded-concurrency AI calls
  review.js           the review list and applying renames
  history.js          persisted rename log, powers undo
  naming.js           model output -> safe filename
  naming.test.js      unit tests for the above (node --test)
  settings.js         persisted settings + credential-store key access
  platform.js         the per-platform facts the UI words itself from
src-tauri/
  src/lib.rs          commands, tray/menu bar, window behaviour
  src/watcher.rs      folder watching with write-completion detection
  src/ai.rs           OpenAI-compatible vision requests
  src/imaging.rs      downscale + JPEG + base64
  src/files.rs        scanning, collision-safe rename, undo
  src/secrets.rs      Credential Manager / Keychain
  src/toast.rs        WinRT toast on Windows, plain notification elsewhere
  tauri.conf.json     shared config, plus the Windows bundle
  tauri.macos.conf.json
                      merged over it when building for macOS
  Info.plist          macOS folder-access usage descriptions

Platform-specific behaviour is #[cfg]-gated in Rust and driven off platform.js in the frontend, so neither side sniffs the user agent or assumes a platform. docs/MACOS.md lists what differs on macOS and why.

Not in v1

Deliberately left out to keep the first release shippable:

  • Managing local models for you (installing, downloading, VRAM detection) — point the base URL at Ollama or LM Studio instead
  • Mac App Store distribution
  • Notarised macOS builds (they need a paid Apple Developer ID)
  • Linux — the Rust side is #[cfg]-gated rather than Windows-only now, but nothing there has been built or tested
  • File types other than images

These may be implemented in the future, who knows?

贡献

欢迎提出问题和拉取请求。 The most useful contributions right now are real-world reports of endpoints or models that misbehave, and screenshots that produce bad names.
